messages:
FinanceOps: Heads up — automated budget alert for asia-east1 GPU spend fired at 00:42 UTC. Overnight charges ~ $12.3k and the alert couldn't map to an owner. Need quick attribution and a short-term cost assignment before EOD. :warning:
eng-platform: Can you paste the billing export dataset name? I can run a rollup query now. :mag:
FinanceOps: dataset is billing_view.gcp_billing_export_v1_012345. Quick SQL I usually run:
```sql
SELECT project_id AS project, sku_description, SUM(cost) AS cost
FROM `billing_view.gcp_billing_export_v1_012345.gcp_billing_export_v1_*`
WHERE usage_start_time >= TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 1 DAY)
GROUP BY project_id, sku_description
ORDER BY cost DESC
LIMIT 50;
```
eng-platform: running that now.
eng-platform: result preview — top lines: playground-experiments: $9.46k, team-alpha-dev: $1.8k, infra-test: $700. playground-experiments is 77% of the spike.
FinanceOps: who owns playground-experiments? @amanda? :eyes:
amanda: that's on my team. Strange — we had a project quota and a daily cap. I'll check job history and quotas.
eng-sre: quick note: we saw a preemption wave in asia-east1 around 23:50 UTC so some pipelines switched to on-demand and kept GPUs for longer. That can cause huge unexpected costs. I pushed a temporary alert to detect preemption->on-demand failover. :white_check_mark:
FinanceOps: ok — looks like we need both attribution and an interim cost reassignment. If we can confirm playground-experiments is responsible, can we tag the overnight cost to "R&D-temp" cost center and then retrocharge?
amanda: yes — I found a runaway batch job started by Jenkins job 4829. Command matched: `kubectl apply -f batch-large-gpu.yaml --namespace=playground`. I'm stopping the job now and scaling the node pool down.
amanda: quick command I ran to inspect instances:
```bash
gcloud compute instances list --filter="name~playground" --format="table(name,labels,gpu_count)"
```
eng-platform: nice catch. Can you paste the affected VM IDs so we can reconcile on the invoice?
amanda: affected VMs: gp-asia-00123, gp-asia-00124, gp-asia-00125. Attached GPUs: 8,8,4 respectively.
eng-sre: preemption metric shows a 60% preemption spike from 23:45–00:05 which caused the controller to restart pods on on-demand instances; that explains the surge. We should look at autoscaler fallback policy — switching to on-demand without kill-switch increased runtime.
FinanceOps: Can we get the precise cost numbers to allocate before EOD? I need a figure to put on the chargeback ticket. :alarm_clock:
amanda: final attributable cost for playground-experiments during window 23:30–01:00 = $9,460. I'll own the retrocharge and create the PR to move the cost to team R&D pool. Also adding a quota override to avoid repeats.
billing-bot: Ticket created: BILL-987 — "Immediate cost reassignment: playground-experiments overnight GPU spike". Assignee: amanda. Due: today 23:59 UTC.
product-ops: moving forward, can we have a pre-deploy checklist for large GPU jobs that requires a cost-center tag and a deploy approval from cost owners? This thread is a good trigger.
amanda: +1. I'll open a PR for a lightweight gating policy in CI.
FinanceOps: thanks everyone. Once BILL-987 has the final invoice line items, I'll issue a temporary transfer to R&D and follow up with a retro charge. Please ping if the numbers change. :thumbsup:
